analysis.evidence: חֲנוֹךְ is the subject, and אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים means “with God.” The verse repeats the wording of Genesis 5:22, where Enoch walks with God for three hundred years, describing his continuing way of life.
analysis.morphology: וַ is the prefixed conjunction. יִּתְהַלֵּךְ is Hithpael wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular.
analysis.sense: conduct one’s life in fellowship with God

analysis.evidence: חֲנוֹךְ is the subject of וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ, “he walked.” The statement that Enoch walked with God repeats Genesis 5:22 and refers to the same Enoch whom Genesis 5:18 identifies as Jared’s son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ חֲנוֹךְ אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים (“Enoch walked with God”), חֲנוֹךְ is the subject of וַיִּתְהַלֵּךְ, and אֶת introduces הָאֱלֹהִים as the one with whom Enoch walked.
analysis.morphology: A preposition with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים, אֶת means “with” and identifies God as the one with whom Enoch walked. The same אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb לָקַח in כִּי לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, “for God took him.”
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a masculine plural common noun in the absolute state. The noun refers to God in the singular.

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers to Enoch. The following clause כִּי לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, “because God took him,” explains why he was no longer present.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ plus the negative existential particle אֵין with a third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, “God took him,” as the reason for וְאֵינֶנּוּ, “and he was no more.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and אֹתוֹ refers to Enoch. The כִּי clause explains וְאֵינֶנּוּ, “he was no longer there”: God had taken him away.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In כִּי לָקַח אֹתוֹ אֱלֹהִים, “because God took him,” אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the masculine singular verb לָקַח. It refers to the same God with whom Enoch walked earlier in the verse.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular reference and no prefix or suffix.
